front_blocks.md: Define **electronic configuration**.

back_blocks.md: An **electronic configuration** is the arrangement of **electrons** in the **shells** and **subshells** of an atom. In the ground state, electrons fill from the lowest energy shell upward.

cards.front_md: Define **electronic configuration**.

front_blocks.md: Shell *n* = 3 can hold a maximum of **..........**  electrons, and shell *n* = 4 can hold a maximum of **..........**  electrons.

back_blocks.md: Shell *n* = 3 can hold a maximum of **18** electrons, and shell *n* = 4 can hold a maximum of **32** electrons.

cards.front_md: Shell *n* = 3 can hold a maximum of **..........**  electrons, and shell *n* = 4 can hold a maximum of **..........**  electrons.
cards.back_md: Shell *n* = 3 can hold a maximum of **18** electrons, and shell *n* = 4 can hold a maximum of **32** electrons.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The *n* = 3 principal quantum **shell** can hold a maximum of 8 **electrons**.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The *n* = 3 shell can hold a maximum of **18 electrons**. The capacity increases with shell number: *n* = 1 holds 2, *n* = 2 holds 8, *n* = 3 holds 18 and *n* = 4 holds 32.

front_blocks.md: Why is the **4s orbital** filled before the **3d orbital**?

back_blocks.md: The **4s orbital** has slightly lower **energy** than the **3d orbital**, despite being in a higher principal quantum shell. Electrons always fill the **lowest energy** orbital first, so 4s fills before 3d.

front_blocks.md: Define **orbital**.

back_blocks.md: An **orbital** is a region of space around the **nucleus** where there is a high probability of finding an **electron**. Each orbital can hold a maximum of **2 electrons**.

cards.front_md: Define **orbital**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A higher **principal quantum number** corresponds to a higher energy **shell**.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
As the **principal quantum number** (*n*) increases, the shell is further from the nucleus and has higher **energy**. Electrons in outer shells are held less tightly than those in inner shells.

cards.back_md:
**True.**

front_blocks.md: What is the **ground state** of an atom?

back_blocks.md: The **ground state** is the most stable electronic configuration of an atom, in which electrons occupy the **lowest available energy** subshells first (starting with 1s).

cards.front_md: What is the **ground state** of an atom?
cards.back_md: The **ground state** is the most stable electronic configuration of an atom, in which electrons occupy the **lowest available energy** subshells first (starting with 1s).

front_blocks.md: In order of increasing energy, the subshells are: s, **..........**,  **..........**  and **..........**.

back_blocks.md: In order of increasing energy, the subshells are: s, **p**, **d** and **f**.

cards.front_md: In order of increasing energy, the subshells are: s, **..........**,  **..........**  and **..........**.

front_blocks.md: How many **electrons** can the *n* = 2 shell hold, and why?

back_blocks.md: The *n* = 2 shell can hold **8 electrons**. It contains one **s** subshell (2 electrons) and one **p** subshell (6 electrons), giving a total of 2 + 6 = **8 electrons**.

cards.front_md: How many **electrons** can the *n* = 2 shell hold, and why?
cards.back_md: The *n* = 2 shell can hold **8 electrons**. It contains one **s** subshell (2 electrons) and one **p** subshell (6 electrons), giving a total of 2 + 6 = **8 electrons**.

front_blocks.md: Define **degenerate** orbitals.

back_blocks.md: **Degenerate** orbitals are orbitals within the same **subshell** that have identical **energies**. For example, the three **p** orbitals (p<sub>x</sub>, p<sub>y</sub> and p<sub>z</sub>) within a given shell are all degenerate.

front_blocks.md: The **p** subshell holds a maximum of **..........**  electrons and the **d** subshell holds a maximum of **..........**  electrons.

back_blocks.md: The **p** subshell holds a maximum of **6** electrons and the **d** subshell holds a maximum of **10** electrons.

cards.front_md: The **p** subshell holds a maximum of **..........**  electrons and the **d** subshell holds a maximum of **..........**  electrons.
cards.back_md: The **p** subshell holds a maximum of **6** electrons and the **d** subshell holds a maximum of **10** electrons.

front_blocks.md: How many **orbitals** does the **p** subshell contain, and what are they called?

back_blocks.md: The **p** subshell contains **3 orbitals**, labelled p<sub>x</sub>, p<sub>y</sub> and p<sub>z</sub>. Each orbital holds up to 2 electrons, so the p subshell holds a maximum of **6 electrons** in total.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The **p** orbitals are **spherical** in shape.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **p** orbitals are **dumbbell-shaped**, with two lobes on opposite sides of the nucleus. It is the **s** orbital that is spherical.

front_blocks.md: Describe the shape and size trend of **s** orbitals.

back_blocks.md: The **s** orbital is **spherical** in shape. Its size increases with the **principal quantum number**. The 3s orbital is larger than the 2s, which is larger than the 1s.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All orbitals within the same **subshell** have the same **energy**.

back_blocks.md: **True.**

Orbitals within the same subshell are **degenerate**, meaning they have identical energies. For example, p<sub>x</sub>, p<sub>y</sub> and p<sub>z</sub> all have the same energy within a given **p** subshell.

front_blocks.md: How are the three **p** orbitals arranged relative to one another?

back_blocks.md: The three **p** orbitals (p<sub>x</sub>, p<sub>y</sub> and p<sub>z</sub>) are oriented along the **x**, **y** and **z** axes. They point **perpendicular** to one another, so the lobes of each orbital are at right angles to the other two.

back_blocks.md: The **s** subshell contains **1** orbital, the **p** subshell contains **3** orbitals and the **d** subshell contains **5** orbitals.

front_blocks.md: How many **electrons** can the **f** subshell hold, and why?

back_blocks.md: The **f** subshell can hold **14 electrons**. It contains **7 orbitals**, and each orbital holds a maximum of **2 electrons** (7 × 2 = 14).

front_blocks.md: Define **electron box notation**.

back_blocks.md: An **electron box notation** is a diagram showing electrons as arrows within boxes, each box representing one orbital, used to display electron spin and filling order.

front_blocks.md: Electrons occupy the **..........**-energy orbitals available first. Within a sub-shell, electrons fill **..........**  orbitals before pairing.

back_blocks.md: Electrons occupy the **lowest**-energy orbitals available first. Within a sub-shell, electrons fill **separate** orbitals before pairing.

cards.front_md: Electrons occupy the **..........**-energy orbitals available first. Within a sub-shell, electrons fill **..........**  orbitals before pairing.

front_blocks.md: Why do two electrons in the same orbital have opposite spins?

back_blocks.md: Opposite spins minimise electron repulsion (spin-pair repulsion), making this the lower-energy arrangement.

cards.front_md: Why do two electrons in the same orbital have opposite spins?

front_blocks.md: Why do electrons in the same sub-shell occupy separate orbitals before pairing?

back_blocks.md: Occupying separate orbitals reduces electron-electron repulsion, giving a lower overall energy.

front_blocks.md: Define **shorthand electron configuration**.

back_blocks.md: A **shorthand electron configuration** is a way of writing electron arrangement using the symbol of the previous noble gas in square brackets to represent inner electrons, followed by the remaining sub-shells. For example, potassium: [Ar] 4s<sup>1</sup>.

back_blocks.md: Transition metals fill the **4s** sub-shell before **3d**, but lose electrons from **4s** first when forming ions.

front_blocks.md: What is the shorthand electron configuration of chromium (Cr, Z = 24)?

back_blocks.md: [Ar] 3d<sup>5</sup> 4s<sup>1</sup>. The expected [Ar] 3d<sup>4</sup> 4s<sup>2</sup> is not observed because a half-filled 3d sub-shell is energetically favourable, so one electron is promoted from 4s.
